comments.why: Surprising way pi appears in the Mandelbrot set
comments.text: My absolute favorite numberphile video is how pi occurs in a peculiar way with Riemann Zeta/Mandelbrot. Maybe it only amazes me because I don’t have a PhD in math, but it just seemed so strange how pi shows up in this video. [VIDEO]

comments.author: throwawaymath
comments.why: Explains how pi emerges from the Mandelbrot set
comments.text: When you begin with z = k i - 0.75, you can obtain an arbitrarily good approximation of pi by multiplying the p for which f_p(z) = z^2 + z diverges by k . The approximation increases in precision as k tends to 0. There's a neat video explaining it here: [VIDEO]
